output.narrative: The attacker gains initial access through unknown means. The first malicious action observed was downloading and running an executable named sandcat-linux using curl from the attackers controlled domain (124.223.85.207). This is likely used as a backdoor. Then it executes various commands within the Linux environment to gather information related to the CPU Usage of the machine in question (defense evasion), hostname, description, language, timezone etc., indicating they have reached the discovery phase. Additionally, SQL Tool Updater Utility has been downloaded and executed multiple times with different parameters such as port numbers, IP addresses, user names, passwords etc. They attempt to list all open TCP sockets on the target machine, execute code with elevated privileges, perform syscalls, and other general reconnaissance activities which suggests it may be part of an exploitation tactic. Furthermore, they also performed the following operations during this time-period: gathered data on the machines hardware configuration, inspected details regarding memory and disk usage statistics, port scanning, established multiple low-level socket communications between processes, resulted in an increase of messages directed toward the kernel space. All this corroborates the idea that there might exist some form of hidden persistence mechanism implemented in order to gain persistent control over resources.
